finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::array date/time oids are not covered by raw_text_oids, so timestamp[]/date[]/timestamptz[] columns are still parsed into js dates using the node runtime timezone
evidence: RAW_TEXT_OIDS at packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts:20-24 contains only the scalar OIDs types.builtins.DATE (1082), TIMESTAMP (1114) and TIMESTAMPTZ (1184); pg-types' builtins map has no array entries, so the array OIDs (_timestamp 1115, _date 1182, _timestamptz 1185) fall through to getDefaultParser at line 35, which is pg-types' parseDateArray and yields JS `Date` elements. For `timestamp without time zone`, pg-types interprets the naive text in the Node process timezone, and toCell (readonly.ts:31 → JSON.stringify → Date#toJSON, UTC ISO) then renders the shifted instant — the exact defect the comment on lines 18-19 claims to remove, plus a rendering inconsistency versus the raw-text scalars (SET TimeZone='UTC' only affects Postgres' text output for tz-aware types, not the client-side Date construction for naive timestamps). I rated it minor rather than major because it only affects array-typed date/time columns, which are an uncommon shape in query results, and the change is still a net improvement for the scalar cases.
